Continue Checkpoint 6 — React Inventory + Search.

Please inspect the current frontend first. CP6 functionality is already implemented and reviewed; I only want this final UI layout improvement.

- Keep the dark Global Inventory navigation sidebar unchanged.
- Move the existing Filter frames panel from the left to a horizontal section above the inventory table.
- Search on top; below it: Status, Media type, Environment, Format, Region, with Clear all easily accessible.
- Make the filters responsive/wrapping and give the table the full available content width.
- Status stays dropdown: All / LIVE / INACTIVE.
- Keep the other filters as free-text inputs.
- Preserve existing behaviour: ~300ms debounce for text filters, immediate Status, request/loading race handling, pagination, error/loading/empty states and accessibility fixes.

Keep this mainly a layout/CSS change. Do not change backend/API, add dependencies, hard-code new filter values, or refactor working logic.

Afterwards run lint, production build and git diff --check, then report any MUST FIX or SHOULD FIX findings.
I’ll inspect the existing component structure and styles first, then make the smallest layout/CSS-focused change and run the requested checks.

I have tested the feature i found small bug

Please fix the datalist filter behaviour frontend-only.

For Media type, Environment, Format, and Region:

- typing should only filter/show matching suggestions locally
- do not call the backend while the user is typing a partial value
- call the backend only after the user selects a valid suggestion
- clearing the input should clear that backend filter
- keep Status immediate
- keep the main Search q debounce unchanged

Example:
typing "R" in Environment should show suggestions such as ROADSIDE, but must not send environment=R.
Only after selecting ROADSIDE should the API request use environment=ROADSIDE.

Do not change backend/API contracts, pagination, loading/request logic, layout, or dependencies.

Afterwards run lint, production build and git diff --check.

I found the cause: the four datalist input values were still included in the shared 300ms request effect. I’ll keep those values as local drafts, remove them from that effect, and commit a filter only when its value exactly matches an available suggestion—or when it becomes empty. The main search debounce remains unchanged.
